title: 6 Safe Fasting Precautions For Pregnant Women
text:
6 Safe Fasting Precautions For Pregnant Women By Kalwyna Rathod 6 Safe Fasting Precautions For Pregnant Women
 Oct 29, 2026 1. Get Medical Clearance
 Fasting is not advised in the first trimester or if you have nausea/vomiting, gestational diabetes, or a high-risk pregnancy. Never fast without your gynaecologist’s approval!
 Source: Pexels 2. Stay Hydrated
 If your gynaecologist advises against observing a complete fast without water, discuss a modified fast where you can have water, coconut water, and juices. Aim for 2.5-3 litres of fluid in 24 hours.
 source-shutterstock 3. Snack On Fasting-Friendly Foods
 Instead of going without food for 12+ hours, keep gaps no longer than 3-4 hours. Snack on nutritious foods like fruits, milk, curd, makhana, nuts, etc if your tradition allows.
 source-shutterstock femina You may also like
 8 Calcium Absorption Mistakes... 6 Daily Habits That Protect Bone... 8 Circadian Reset Habits After... 6 Daily Habits That Protect Bone... 4. Don’t Exert Yourself
 Pregnancy lowers blood sugar and blood pressure. Avoid prolonged standing, long hours in kitchen heat, or heavy work while fasting. Take frequent breaks, and keep a family member around.
 Source: Pexels 5. Watch Out For Warning Signs
 Break your fast right away if you experience dizziness, excessive thirst, very dark urine, less foetal movement, palpitations, nausea, or contractions. Contact your doctor immediately.
 source-shutterstock 6. Break The Fast Gradually
 Start with water, then have some fruit. Eat a balanced meal with protein, complex carbohydrates, and fibre. Avoid excessive salty, fried, or heavy foods to prevent acidity and blood sugar spikes.
